children: Worthington Steel said the DPLTA with Kloeckner was not approved by Kloeckner shareholders, so it will not take effect. WS keeps ~62% of Kloeckner, continues financial consolidation, and will pursue synergies within existing governance.
Limits WS’s control and near-term synergy capture; governance remains constrained.
No domination/P&L transfer means fewer levers for cash upstreaming and integration.
Majority control persists; strategic combination remains viable long term.
WS’s reported results still include Kloeckner; no change to financing.
Integration benefits may be slower, affecting timeline of value realization.

This is a setback to WS’s planned tighter control after acquiring a majority of Kloeckner in June 2026. A renewed vote, alternative governance steps, or revised terms enabling greater control would turn this into a larger catalyst.
